thread:
Irene (SRE): paging: increase in 5xxs hitting /v1/generate from us-west-2 services, started ~10:14 PDT. Alerts from dashboards and customer p99 latency spike.
Mike (Oncall): I'm on it, grabbing logs and checking ELB target health now.
IncidentBot: incident created: INC-2026-0423-01 | Sev2 | source=Monitoring | channel=#incidents | assignees=@Mike (Oncall)
Mike (Oncall): ELB (app/my-app-elb) showing intermittent target unhealthy in us-west-2b. TargetGroup health flips between healthy/unhealthy ~1m intervals. Not all AZs affected.
Jamal (Runtime Eng): this smells like ENI/conntrack or control plane API throttling in that AZ. Any EC2/ENI events?
Mike (Oncall): checking EC2 console -> several instances in us-west-2b reported ENI detach events 10:12-10:16. CloudTrail shows AttachNetworkInterface errors `RequestLimitExceeded` around same time.
Irene (SRE): ok that's consistent with control-plane throttling causing temporary detaches and target failures. Customer impact: several active customers seeing aborted streams and 502/504s. Sarah can you surface any high-touch min customers?
Sarah (Product): flagged 3 paying customers on support side, they've seen session drop and partial responses. Support already emailed customers A & B with temporary mitigation steps.
Mike (Oncall): mitigation plan: 1) reduce traffic to us-west-2b via Route53 weighted routing shift to other AZ endpoints 2) increase ELB connection draining + lower deregistration delay 3) raise health check threshold window to avoid flapping 4) open case with AWS support (on it). Any objections?
Jamal (Runtime Eng): +1. For draining, set deregistration_delay to 60 -> avoids immediate failover. Also add a short-term prefix KV cache bypass for calls routed away from affected AZ to prevent heavy retries.
Irene (SRE): do the Route53 shift now; set weight for us-west-2b to 10% and others to 45%/45%. Also reduce Route53 TTL to 30s to let changes propagate fast.
Mike (Oncall): executing: `aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id Z12345 --change-batch file://shift.json` (applied). Added note in channel: TTL now 30s. :white_check_mark:
OpsBot: Deploy event: route53-weight-update completed by mike_oncall at 2026-04-23T17:20:10Z
Mike (Oncall): updating target group deregistration_delay to 60: `aws elbv2 modify-target-group-attributes --target-group-arn arn:aws:... --attributes Key=deregistration_delay.timeout_seconds,Value=60` -> applied to all TGs in us-west-2.
Jamal (Runtime Eng): changed health check healthy threshold from 2 -> 4 and unhealthy threshold 2 -> 4 to reduce flapping. Command and result attached.
Irene (SRE): started traffic steering. Metrics show 5xxs dropping in 2m. p50/p90 latency trending back. Monitoring: keep an eye for control plane events.
AWS Support: Case #123456789 opened. We've engaged control plane team, seeing elevated API throttling in us-west-2b impacting ENI attach/detach. We're prioritizing.
Mike (Oncall): customers still seeing some residual stream resets. Rolling a temporary rollback of a recent runtime change that increased ENI churn (decreased ephemeral port reuse) — Jamal can you coordinate config rollback?
Jamal (Runtime Eng): rolling back runtime build 2026-04-22-19 -> reverting conn reuse to previous flags. Patch deploy started (canary 10% us-west-2a first). Logs:```
- flag conn_reuse=false (new) -> now conn_reuse=true (rollback)
- restarting 2/3 canary hosts
```
Irene (SRE): nice. Also add an autoscaling-provisioned buffer: spin up 8 additional warm instances in healthy AZs to absorb shifted traffic.
Mike (Oncall): started ASG scale-up in us-west-2a/c: `aws autoscaling set-desired-capacity --auto-scaling-group-name app-asg-usw2a --desired-capacity 28` -> triggered.
Sarah (Product): notified customers about mitigation and asked support to monitor for resumed errors. :pray:
IncidentBot: oncall handoff scheduled at 18:00 PDT to @Irene (SRE).
Irene (SRE): I'm taking over for the on-call window. Summary so far: control-plane API throttling in us-west-2b causing ENI detach -> ELB target unhealthy flaps -> client 5xxs. Mitigations applied: Route53 weight shift, lowered TTL, TG health thresholds increased, deregistration delay increased, runtime rollback, ASG buffer, AWS case opened. Continue monitoring.
Mike (Oncall): leaving notes in runbook and outputting timeline. Handing off to @Irene.
Mike (Oncall): log snippet of interesting errors:```
2026-04-23T17:13:02Z WARN ec2 AttachNetworkInterface RequestLimitExceeded
2026-04-23T17:13:07Z ERROR target/10.0.2.45 Health check failed: connection reset
2026-04-23T17:14:21Z INFO elb deregister instance i-0abcd1234
```
Irene (SRE): tracking next actions: 1) follow up with AWS support for mitigation ETA 2) keep Route53 low weight until AWS confirms stable 3) if control plane persists >2h, move to AZ isolation plan (drain and cordon us-west-2b fully) 4) prepare customer status update if impact exceeds 30m more.
AWS Support: we have a mitigation underway; control plane team advises rate-limiting improvement rolling within 30-45 mins. We'll update case and provide timeline.
Irene (SRE): noted. I'll prepare a short status for customers now and update at +30m if degraded persists.
Sarah (Product): please include note that we are not changing data plane model behavior, only routing and runtime rollback. Customers appreciate clarity.
Irene (SRE): publishing status update to support via email and to incident page. Draft: "We've identified an intermittent control-plane event in AWS us-west-2b that's causing some instances to briefly detach network interfaces which in turn causes ELB targets to flap. We've shifted traffic away from the affected AZ, adjusted load balancer health checks, and rolled back a recent runtime change. We're partnered with AWS and monitoring closely. Next update in 30 minutes or on significant change."
Mike (Oncall): adding annotation to Grafana charts and to incident timeline.
IncidentBot: annotation added by mike_oncall at 2026-04-23T17:38:00Z
Irene (SRE): will keep this thread as the single source of truth. Paging policy: if error rate rises above 3% globally or another AZ shows similar events, escalate to Sev1 and page exec team.
Jamal (Runtime Eng): any logs that show TCP resets vs app errors? Might be helpful to decisively rule conntrack exhaustion.
Mike (Oncall): capturing tcpdump from healthy host and affected host, uploading to S3: s3://redwood-incident-dumps/1758123456/tcpdump-10.0.2.45.pcap
Irene (SRE): good. If AWS control plane mitigation is confirmed, plan to gradually restore Route53 weights back to even over 20 minutes and reduce TTL back to normal.
AWS Support: update: mitigation in progress; observed reduction in API errors in last 5 minutes. We will continue to monitor.
Irene (SRE): monitoring shows dropped 5xxs to baseline and client sessions resuming. Marking incident as mitigated but keeping open for follow-up.
Sarah (Product): thanks team. I'll coordinate post-incident customer comms and include timeline + root cause hypothesis pending AWS RCA.
Mike (Oncall): closing notes: handoff completed, runbook updated, ticket with AWS attached.
Irene (SRE): incident status: mitigated -> will set P0 follow-up for RCA and adjust our runtime to avoid creating additional ENI churn. Thanks all. :heart:
